title: Accept the ai.ubq.fi #1162 interface change in the VPS release bridge
body:
ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#1162, which fixes ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#1146, was merged as [`6c3afe42`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1). It makes the pinned driver's import graph loadable by Deno. That satisfies the "the driver offers a Deno-loadable lock" option in #150's acceptance.

It also adds host requirements for the bridge that neither #150 nor #161 records, and it leaves release preparation Bun-only. The ai.ubq.fi side of that gap is tracked in ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#1178.

## What changed

| | Before #1162 (ai.ubq.fi `9f98f131`) | After #1162 (`6c3afe42`) |
|---|---|---|
| Driver import graph | `ops/vps-release-journal.ts` imports `ops/deploy-lock.ts`, whose line 2 imports `bun:ffi`. `ops/io.ts` runs commands through `Bun.spawn`. Deno fails with `Unsupported scheme "bun"`. | No module reachable from `ops/vps-release-driver.ts`, `ops/vps-release-metrics.ts` or `ops/vps-metrics-storage.ts` names a `bun:` module. The Bun FFI lock moved to `ops/deploy-lock-bun.ts`. It loads through a URL-built dynamic import, and only when `globalThis.Bun` is defined. |
| Deploy lock ([`ops/deploy-lock.ts:11-47`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/deploy-lock.ts#L11-L47)), taken by `withVpsDeployLock` for every driver operation and for each `createVpsJoinFileStorage` load and save | Bun FFI `flock` | On Deno it uses `Deno.open` and `FsFile.tryLockSync(true)`: the same `flock(LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB)`, polled every 100 ms with a 240 s deadline. The lock file must be mode `0600` and owned by `Deno.uid()`, so the host needs `--allow-sys=uid` plus read and write on `<root>/.data`. Without `--allow-sys=uid`, every acquisition throws `NotCapable` and no operation runs. It also needs a Deno that has `FsFile.tryLockSync` (verified on 2.9.7). |
| Command runner: `runVpsCommand` ([`ops/vps-release-driver.ts:44`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/vps-release-driver.ts#L44)), which goes through `command` and `runOutput` ([`ops/io.ts:98-120`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/io.ts#L98-L120)) | `Bun.spawn` | `Deno.Command` on Deno, which needs `--allow-run`. The normal runner needs no env grant. Sparse mode, used only by release preparation, reads `PATH`. |
| Release payload preparation | Bun-only | Still Bun-only. On Deno, `prepare` for a candidate not already under `.data/releases/<sha>` throws `ReferenceError: Bun is not defined`. The only way around it is a bridge-supplied `preparePayload` that avoids `Bun.version`, and ai.ubq.fi has none yet (ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#1178, item 1). |
| Ingress helpers | `ops/deploy.ts` | Moved unchanged to `ops/vps-ingress.ts`, except that `ensureCaddyIngressReady` lost its default arguments. |

One more requirement predates #1162. `runVpsJournalCommand` ([`ops/vps-journal-reader.ts:113`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/vps-journal-reader.ts#L113)) spawns through `node:child_process`, and Deno's implementation of it reads `NODE_V8_COVERAGE` even when the child gets an explicit `env`. I checked with Deno 2.9.7. With only `--allow-run`, an `execFile` call throws `NotCapable: Requires env access to "NODE_V8_COVERAGE"`. Adding `--allow-env=NODE_V8_COVERAGE` lets it run.

## Sentinel files involved

I checked these with `git grep` on `development` (`87e28fd4`) and on the #150 branch `origin/codex/master-plan-gfa795549e5` (`8e34ff6f`):
- `src/host/vps-release.ts:291` on `development` and `:389` on the #150 branch call `createVpsDeploymentDriver({...})` without `preparePayload`. The driver therefore falls back to the Bun-only `prepareReleasePayload`.
- Nothing imports `ops/deploy.ts`, `ops/vps-ingress.ts` or `ops/deploy-lock*.ts`, and nothing names `ensureCaddyIngressReady`, so the ingress move needs no change here. `src/release/vps-port.ts` hashes the whole pinned release tree, so the two new files need no list update.
- No file in this repository sets the bridge's Deno permission flags. The forced command is installed by the owner (`ops/vps-release-bridge.ts:1`), so the permission changes are an installation step, not a code change.

## Impact

Nothing is broken live today. `sentinel-release` is disabled, and the bridge's pinned driver is `21e4a2a9`.

Once the driver is re-pinned at or after `6c3afe42`, these are the risks:
- **Permissions.** Without `--allow-sys=uid`, every locked driver operation and every metrics checkpoint load or save fails with `NotCapable`, so every VPS release is refused. Without `--allow-env=NODE_V8_COVERAGE`, journal reads fail, so metrics cannot sample.
- **Preparation.** Every release whose candidate is not already under `.data/releases/<sha>` is refused at `prepare`. This lasts until a Deno-safe `preparePayload` exists and the bridge passes it.

## Acceptance

- The bridge host grants:
  - `--allow-sys=uid`;
  - `--allow-run`;
  - read and write on the target root's `.data`;
  - `--allow-env=NODE_V8_COVERAGE`, plus `PATH` if it uses sparse preparation.

  It also runs a Deno that has `FsFile.tryLockSync`.
- Once ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#1178 item 1 provides a Deno-safe `preparePayload`, the bridge passes it to `createVpsDeploymentDriver`. Until then, record that releases can only be driven for candidates already prepared on the VPS.
- The interface pin test asked for in #150 also loads and exercises the pinned driver under the exact Deno permissions the bridge host uses. Then a missing grant fails CI instead of failing at release time.
- Land this together with #150 and #161.

title: Follow-up from #1156 (issue #1132): track the two owner-only items it closed over, and tighten the live-relay docs and runner test
body:
PR #1156 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1156) fixed issue #1132. It was merged from head `57bbd2f1` in commit 0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e). This issue collects the review findings from that PR that still apply on development.

All line numbers are at the merge commit `0d726874`, which is also the current development tip. The review found nothing at P0 or P1.

## 1. Two owner-only items from #1132 are now tracked nowhere (P2)

**Where.**
- [`docs/log-retention-and-quota-runway-2026-08-25.md:178`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/docs/log-retention-and-quota-runway-2026-08-25.md#L178) says the hard cap was "declined by the owner on 2026-10-16 (issue #139)".
- [`scripts/test-network.ts:150-152`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/scripts/test-network.ts#L150-L152) and [`README.md:24`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/README.md?plain=1#L24): a Darwin live run refuses every non-loopback `BASE_URL`, including the default `https://ai.ubq.fi`.

**Problem.** #1156's `Resolves #1132` closed #1132 as completed on merge (2026-10-18 01:56Z). Only an owner can act on two of its items, and #1156 listed both only under Known limitations in its PR body:
- **#1073 item 2.** The retention doc cites a decline by the owner on 2026-10-16 in #139. That decline is recorded nowhere: #139 has only bot comments, and `docs/DECISIONS.md` has no entry for #139 or the hard cap. #139 is still closed as "completed", but no eviction was built.
- **#1077 item 2.** On macOS, live e2e can reach only a host-loopback `BASE_URL`. The default `https://ai.ubq.fi` fails closed at validation. #1077 left a scoped CONNECT relay (or similar) for non-loopback destinations as an owner decision.

**Failure scenario.** Now that #1132 is closed, these items appear only in a merged PR's description. A reader who follows the retention doc's "(issue #139)" citation finds no decline, and #139's "completed" close reason suggests eviction was built. No open issue asks for the macOS decision, so it is never made.

**Suggested fix.**
- Owner: record the 2026-10-16 decline, either in a comment on #139 or in a short dated `docs/DECISIONS.md` entry. Optionally, change #139's close reason to "not planned".
- Owner: decide on non-loopback live e2e for macOS. Either accept the limit (`README.md:24` already describes it), or open a task for a destination-scoped CONNECT relay.
- No code change is needed until the owner decides.

## 2. No test checks that the runner's main loop wraps each file in `withLiveRelayParent` (P3)

**Where.**
- [`scripts/test-runner.ts:308`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/scripts/test-runner.ts#L308): `main()` calls `withLiveRelayParent(item.policy, (policy) => runFile(...))`.
- The helper is at [`scripts/test-runner.ts:174-182`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/scripts/test-runner.ts#L174-L182).
- The SIGKILL test at [`tests/live-network-policy.test.ts:93-129`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/tests/live-network-policy.test.ts#L93-L129) calls the helper directly. No other test imports `scripts/test-runner.ts`.

**Problem.** The test proves that the helper removes a SIGKILLed relay's directory. Nothing proves that `main()` sends each live file through the helper. The review confirmed that a mutation dropping `relayParent` inside the helper fails the test, but a `main()` that bypasses the helper does not.

**Failure scenario.** A later refactor of `main()` goes back to calling `runFile(file.path, item, ...)` directly, and every test stays green. From then on, a live relay killed by timeout escalation, CI cancellation or the OOM killer leaves its `uos-live-*` directory in `TMPDIR`, as it did before #1156.

**Suggested fix.** Use either of these:
- Move the per-file loop out of `main()` into an exported function that takes `runFile` as a parameter. Test it with a stub `runFile` and a live policy, and assert two things: the policy the stub receives has a `relayParent` named `uos-live-run-*`, and that directory is gone after the call returns.
- Run the `e2e` segment against a loopback fixture gateway, SIGKILL the relay in the middle of a file, and assert that no `uos-live-run-*` entry remains in the run's `TMPDIR`.

## 3. The README overstates how isolated the Linux live relay is (P3)

**Where.**
- [`README.md:24`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/README.md?plain=1#L24) says the run uses "a destination-scoped relay that serves only the run's own namespace".
- The actual mechanism is at [`scripts/test-network.ts:170-175`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/scripts/test-network.ts#L170-L175) and [`:233-237`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/scripts/test-network.ts#L233-L237). The host-side relay accepts only streams that start with the per-run key. The forwarder inside the namespace reads the key from fd 3 and puts it in front of every stream it forwards.

**Problem.** The relay serves anything that reaches the key-holding forwarder, not only the run's namespace. A same-user host process can join the run's namespaces and use the forwarder. No document in the repository names this limit. #1156 named only the ptrace limit, and only in its PR body.

**Failure scenario.**
1. A same-user host process opens `/proc/<forwarder pid>/ns/user` and `ns/net`. That needs only `PTRACE_MODE_READ`, which Yama `ptrace_scope=1` does not restrict.
2. As owner of the child user namespace, the process holds `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` there. It can `setns` into the namespace (for example `nsenter -t <pid> -U -n --preserve-credentials`) and connect to the forwarder's listener.
3. The forwarder adds the key, and the stream reaches the approved destination.

This is the same class of limit as ptrace. It does not reopen the threat #1077 fixed: a deterministic test child of another run sits in a sibling user, pid and mount namespace and cannot do this.

**Suggested fix.** Reword the README to "a destination-scoped relay that serves only the run's key-holding forwarder". Then list both namespace entry (`setns` through `/proc/<pid>/ns`) and ptrace by a same-user host process as known limits, in the README or in the relay comment at `scripts/test-network.ts:170-175`.

## 4. The terminal handoff still points to the old name of the narration correction (P3)

**Where.**
- [`docs/handoff/gateway-terminal-truthfulness-handoff-2026-09-21.md:36`](``https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/docs/handoff/gateway-terminal-truthfulness-handoff-2026-09-21.md?plain=1#L36)`` says "the measurement-artifact correction in `docs/DECISIONS.md`".
- [`:47-48`](```https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/docs/handoff/gateway-terminal-truthfulness-handoff-2026-09-21.md?plain=1#L47-L48)``` say "the qualified measurement-artifact correction".
- #1156 renamed the target heading to "CORRECTION: the narration symptom counts are unverified - 2026-09-21" ([`docs/DECISIONS.md:1172`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/docs/DECISIONS.md?plain=1#L1172)). The old name now appears only in a quotation at `:1183`.

**Problem.** Both pointers in the handoff name a heading that no longer exists.

**Failure scenario.** A reader searches `docs/DECISIONS.md` for the name the handoff uses. They find it only inside the quoted old heading in the 2026-10-16 qualification note ("CORRECTION: the narration symptom was itself a measurement artifact"), not as a section heading. No anchor link breaks.

**Suggested fix.** In both places, name the new heading: `See "CORRECTION: the narration symptom counts are unverified - 2026-09-21" in docs/DECISIONS.md`. #602 and #605 cover other parts of the same handoff, so all three can be fixed in one pass.

title: Stop the work queue from arming a timer after stop()
body:
**Severity:** P2. **Where:** [`src/work_queue.ts:91-96`](https://github.com/ubiquity/checkout.ubq.fi/blob/2715f7c155e8de5fea070bbb965b27bfab88c6a9/src/work_queue.ts#L91-L96)

**What happens**

`stop()` can run while the D1 `entries()` scan is waiting on its HTTP response. It clears the timer and sets `started` to false, but the scan's continuation still installs another timer.

So `stop()` resolves while scheduled work can still run handlers or touch a store that has since been closed. A probe that holds the list call open reproduced a handler running after shutdown.

**Expected**

Every continuation in the scheduler checks one lifecycle guard before it arms a timer, runs a handler or touches the store. That guard can be a start/stop generation token, or `started` checked again after each await. `stop()` does not resolve while a handler it could have stopped can still start.

Discovery can answer `discovery.found: true` alongside an `awaiting_payment` invoice. This happens when:

2. that transfer is then reorganised out;
3. `claimPayment()` refreshes the existing locator and clears the payment.

The success branch never looks at the invoice it got back. The caller is told the payment was found when the invoice has no payment. The interleaving was reproduced offline.

`found` is derived from the returned invoice: it is true only if that invoice still carries a current payment. Otherwise discovery keeps scanning. Every other path that reports success (coordinate claim, reconciliation, webhook delivery) should read the returned state the same way.

title: Recover tweet deletion receipts before clearing cleanup on reopen
body:
Severity: P2. Affected revision: `45f7070ff2c2b4330e69dd0a0f84a5a677de94dc`; review round 2 of https://github.com/devpool-directory/devpool-directory/pull/6213.

When a priced source reopens, aggregate clears `cleanupOnly` without resolving whether an earlier tweet deletion succeeded. If deletion succeeded but its receipt commit failed, the persisted `twitter-map.json` still references the deleted tweet, and clearing recovery state suppresses a replacement announcement.

Reproduction:

1. Use fake Twitter and storage clients with an existing announcement and a persisted cleanup marker for a closed source.
2. Let `deleteTweet` succeed, then fail the receipt commit so storage retains the deleted tweet ID and `cleanupOnly` marker.
3. Reopen the source with a Price label and retry aggregate. The affected revision removes the marker, retains the dead tweet mapping, and skips replacement creation.

A controlled two-case comparison passes on `5d1e3498836d4cb899c4070ebe5cf08598e4e65e` and fails on the affected revision with `persisted tweet receipt must not refer to a confirmed deleted tweet`. Local capture: `db7a45d4e385204a4c751b56642a3bca7c154e760ae1a7e67b8ba28776d479cd/67407724-6831-4adb-bbac-9d754241b8d2`.

Acceptance:

- Distinguish a failed deletion from a successful deletion followed by failed receipt publication.
- Resolve and persist deletion recovery, or retain its unresolved state, before clearing cleanup when a priced source reopens.
- Preserve a still-live announcement when deletion failed; restore one valid announcement after confirmed deletion without duplicate posts or a mapping to a deleted tweet.
- Cover both failure windows and repeat retries with fake Twitter calls and persisted receipt assertions.

Files:

- `src/cli/aggregate.ts:219-222`
- `src/twitter/sync-lifecycle.ts`
- `tests/twitter-lifecycle.test.ts`

title: Preserve safe recovery context for interrupted and failed implementation runs
body:
<!-- sentinel:skip -->

Preserve a bounded recovery artifact for failed/interrupted implementation attempts so a trusted continuation can use verified context and partial work after the ephemeral runner exits. This is queued for trusted owner implementation and excluded from autonomous admission; #53 retained advisory failure summaries, which do not establish resumable session state.

Evidence: run [39080597401](https://github.com/ubiquity/sentinel/actions/runs/39080597401), runtime `e48e7e110e7cb2ed3385bf1be5165f05d8a4e481`, had three interrupted turns at the four-million-event-character bound and no candidate bundles. Run [39091929807](https://github.com/ubiquity/sentinel/actions/runs/39091929807) retained an operation-deadline diagnostic without thread/turn identity or candidate. Existing result artifacts are useful accounting evidence but cannot by themselves resume an app-server session or explain/recover partial work. This proposal does not assert that those historical runners or contexts are recoverable.

Acceptance:
- Define a sanitized recovery manifest binding run/attempt, task, reservation, exact base/runtime, submitted model/effort, protocol identity, terminal/settlement evidence and any verified partial patch/checkpoint. Keep advisory context separate from candidate or merge authority.
- Before runner teardown, preserve only the minimum resumable context/partial work through an explicitly scoped private artifact path with bounded retention and integrity checks. Never place raw transcripts, diagnostics, credentials or restricted originals in public Git or issue bodies.
- Prove whether the installed app-server supports resuming from the preserved state on a fresh runner; a thread ID alone is insufficient. When it does not, use a clearly identified fresh continuation with sanitized context instead of claiming a resumed session.
- Resume only after the original process group has settled, revalidate current source/base and target ownership, and use existing durable admission for any new inference. Preserve original charges and history; no duplicate start, silent refund, credential transfer or replay of effects.
- Exercise interruption, teardown, restart, missing/expired/tampered artifacts and changed-base refusal using real production consumers with fake external/model ports. Keep candidate validation, review, CI and publication gates intact.

Files: `src/repair/codex-transport.ts`; `src/repair/model-port-session.ts`; `src/repair/model-port-settlement.ts`; `src/repair/model-port-checkout.ts`; `src/host/matrix-cell.ts`; `src/contracts/matrix-identity.ts`; trusted artifact/recovery consumers.

Source: [owned process close before candidate inspection](https://github.com/ubiquity/sentinel/blob/e48e7e110e7cb2ed3385bf1be5165f05d8a4e481/src/repair/model-port-session.ts#L319); [whole-operation timer](https://github.com/ubiquity/sentinel/blob/e48e7e110e7cb2ed3385bf1be5165f05d8a4e481/src/repair/codex-transport.ts#L236).

title: Retain model token usage and connect it to repair outcomes
body:

Retain available input, output, cached-input and reasoning token usage for each actual model attempt, then connect it to candidate, publication and delivery outcomes. This is queued for trusted owner implementation and excluded from autonomous admission because it changes control-plane contracts and telemetry.

Evidence: the six-hour audit ending 2026-10-18 04:07:06Z found 31 matrix cells, 30 confirmed turns, 17 candidate bundles, four published PRs and zero cohort merges. The retained `ModelRunReceiptV1` in runtime `e48e7e110e7cb2ed3385bf1be5165f05d8a4e481` exposes only duration and event-output characters; it has no token or cost fields. - Capture usage only from supported app-server/provider evidence, with units and provenance. Missing fields remain unavailable; never convert event characters, durations, reservations or cache hits into invented token/billing totals.
- Bind each actual attempt, including retries, failovers, reviews and continuations, to its task, reservation, runtime, submitted model/effort, thread/turn and terminal outcome; avoid duplicate aggregation after restart.
- Report input, output, cached-input and reasoning tokens separately where provided, with explicit coverage/denominators and lifecycle outcomes through protected-path refusal, CI failure, PR publication and merge.
- Keep provider-reported charges separate from estimates. Any estimate records price source/version, model and cache treatment; unknown pricing or usage remains unknown.

title: Follow-up from #1159: coordinate signing-helper migration with active legacy rebuilds (P3)
body:
PR #1159 contains the protected-path follow-ups for #1141. This issue tracks its remaining P3 integration finding, independently reproduced on the reviewed PR source. The conflict with #1156 was resolved in `d0595ccbbb30201689f044649d868f87493415ba`; it is not outstanding work.

### P3: migration cleanup interrupts an in-flight legacy signing helper

**Where:** [`ops/gpg-dsh.sh:136-149`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/d0595ccbbb30201689f044649d868f87493415ba/ops/gpg-dsh.sh#L136-L149), especially the unconditional deletion of the legacy lock and staging/set-aside directories at lines 143-145.

The first invocation of the new per-user-layout helper removes the legacy helper's seed, lock, and staging directories without coordinating with an old helper that is still rebuilding. If an old invocation is paused after acquiring its lock and creating its stage, the new helper deletes both. When the old invocation resumes, its copy or rename fails and that signing exits 2. The new helper succeeds, and subsequent invocations use the new layout normally. This is a one-time upgrade availability failure; the fixture does not demonstrate leaked keys or a bad signature.

**Original finding, preserved from the handoff:**

> The resolution adds code that neither parent has. The legacy cleanup now also removes <uid>.lock, <uid>.new.* and <uid>.old.* under the old $TMPDIR/dsh-gnupg parent (lines 136-149). It does this without holding a lock. It also calls rmdir on the parent even when there is no legacy seed, which reviewed head 2892d609 only did together with removing the seed. The change is disclosed, tested, and consistent with what #1141 intends, so it is integration glue and not a lost behaviour.

> Only possible while upgrading. Suppose a #1139-era installed helper is part-way through a rebuild under $TMPDIR/dsh-gnupg/<uid>.lock when the first call of the newly installed helper runs. The new call deletes that lock and the staging copy, so the old call's mv fails and that one signing exits 2. Every later call works. Reviewed head 2892d609 already had the same window for removing <uid> itself, so the size of the exposure is unchanged.

**Evidence and provenance:**

- Retained source: [`handoff/2026-10-18/reports/protected-finish.json`, `result.check`](https://github.com/ubiquity/sentinel/blob/be02faf40c77fe299c2ed7ffa91fedb00fe43c48/handoff/2026-10-18/reports/protected-finish.json). That review returned PASS, with this P3 and the now-resolved #1156 conflict.
- Original integration reviewed head: `77d3f7c56a86094ecc28c7086e17b2b1efdcb60b`; base: `b24353e5caffc8ec2f935bfcbbe3b7f441dd1aa7`. The retained report does not record the original review command or model identity; those are unavailable, not inferred.
- Independently reproduced on the documentation-resolution head `d0595ccbbb30201689f044649d868f87493415ba` against legacy helper `ed0ecdda85ee261bc8388558bb26c2c86f5ac9a5`, using fixture key strings and fake gpg/gpgconf. The helper is byte-identical on latest-base head `0a7063f994f39d958476d9257c2eef7ce9a7abc9`. A cp wrapper paused the old helper after its lock and stage existed. The new helper exited 0 and removed both; releasing the old helper made it exit 2 with `cp: cannot create regular file .../dsh-gnupg/<uid>.new.*/pubring.kbx: No such file or directory` and `gpg-dsh: cannot copy ... into ...`.
- All fixture paths were under `/workspace/evidence/finish-1159/migration-race-probe`, and the bounded probe did not read or chdir under `/tmp`.
- Actual local review mode was attempted with `codex review --base origin/development` (CLI 0.159.2, printed model `gpt-6.1-sol`, head `d0595ccbbb30201689f044649d868f87493415ba`, base `05260bfe0ac835af0742bc0d116650a6aeb98c74`). It exited 1 before review because authentication returned HTTP 401. No findings were ingested from that failed attempt and no credentials were changed.

**Acceptance:** Coordinate migration with active legacy invocations, or document and enforce an installation quiescence step. Add a deterministic fixture that pauses a live legacy rebuild, invokes the new helper, then resumes the legacy call and proves it is not interrupted. Preserve removal of abandoned legacy key copies, ownership checks, config-file refusal, and the existing per-user layout.

Related #1168 tracks stale-lock recovery and publication races within the helper. This issue is specifically cross-version migration cleanup; do not duplicate that issue's P2/P3 findings. Merging this PR does not install the helper on the owner's Mac.

title: Classify event-scoped CI aborts as configuration defects instead of charging CI-fix retries
body:
When a required CI check fails on a repair candidate's head but the same check passed on the base, `src/repair/ci-rejection.ts` attributes the failure to the candidate and the CI-fix route starts a model retry. On 2026-10-20 every ai.ubq.fi repair PR (#1254–#1258) failed `rust-native`, `rust-wasm` and `validate` because the target workflow only exported `GITHUB_PR_AUTHOR` to its scope job, so downstream jobs aborted with "No Rust work selected" before running anything. The base's green result came from a `push` event with a different scope, so the comparison was not like-for-like. Each CI-fix worker correctly edited the target workflow and was then blocked by the protected-path rule, consuming a CI retry per PR and leaving the records blocked.

Expected: when a head check fails and the only green base evidence comes from a different event type (push vs pull_request), or when the failing job's log matches a configuration-abort signature (no work selected, scope mismatch, setup failure before the test command), classify it as `ci_configuration` instead of a candidate defect: do not charge a CI-fix retry, park the record with the reason, and raise one deduplicated follow-up issue on the target for the owner. Add a fake-transport regression in `tests/repair/` that feeds a green push-event base run and a failed pull_request head run with that log signature and asserts no model start and the parked reason.
